newsitem.title: INDONESIA: U.N. East Timor envoy arrives in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: U.N. East Timor envoy arrives in Jakarta.

text.p: The U.N. secretary-general's special assistant for East Timor, Jamsheed Marker, arrived in Jakarta on Thursday on a visit that was to include a weekend trip to the troubled former Portuguese colony.

Secretary-General Kofi Annan appointed Marker, a former Pakistani ambassador to the United Nations, as his special assistant for East Timor last month in an effort to find an acceptable international solution to the problem of East Timor.
The United Nations said Marker was here on a "familiarisation" visit.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 with tacit Western support after civil war broke out following the withdrawal of Portuguese colonial authorities.
Indonesia incorporated the territory as its 27th province the next July in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
Marker declined to make any statement on his arrival in Jakarta. He was due to see Foreign Minister Ali Alatas and President Suharto later in the day.
Alatas has welcomed Marker's appointment, saying he was a "very experienced" diplomat.

Marker visited Portugal earlier this month and said he hoped talks between Portugal and Indonesia seeking a settlement on East Timor future could be sped up. The U.N.-sponsored talks have dragged on for nearly 15 years.
Meanwhile, a senior U.S. human rights official flew to the East Timorese capital of Dili on Thursday for a two-day visit.
John Shattuck, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labour, will spend two days in East Timor before leaving for Cambodia on Friday night.
He has met several senior officials, including Alatas, during a fact-finding stay in Jakarta.
